metadata.author: hand-authored, Docs/17_phase7_teaching_mode.md M7 / §12.1
metadata.purpose: Answer key for hand-scoring a real teaching-question GENERATION run. Per (concept, band): the acceptable question shape, the reference-answer key points (fact-checked against source at the pinned commit), the required criteria a sound rubric should contain, the anchors that count as valid grounding, and what a generated question MUST NOT say. There is no automated scorer -- a human compares generator output to this, scoring four axes: question relevance, reference-answer factual correctness, criterion validity (each required criterion single-fact and checkable), anchor-resolution rate.
metadata.disclosure: Authored with prior knowledge of Starlette's structure (six phases of building against it) -- NOT blind, same limitation as Phase 2 M5's component gold. Two source concepts here are known to be factually wrong for this commit (redirect_claim: says 302, source is 307; reqbody_claim: says later body() calls return empty, source returns the cached bytes) -- kept deliberately as factual-correctness test cases for the generator.

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question asking the developer to state how Router selects a route for a request.
reference_answer_key_points: Router.app iterates self.routes in registration order
first Match.FULL wins and iteration stops
Match.PARTIAL is a fallback used only if no FULL match (drives 405)
no match -> redirect_slashes retry, else default 404
required_criteria_expected: routes are tried in registration order
the first full match handles the request and the search stops
a partial match is only used when there is no full match
must_not: must not claim routes are ranked by specificity or longest-prefix
must not claim the router gathers all matches then picks the best

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question relating Route.matches' three Match outcomes to what Router.app does with each, or contrasting Route vs Mount matching.
reference_answer_key_points: FULL -> update scope, call handle(), return
PARTIAL -> stash first one, keep scanning
NONE -> ignored
Mount matches a path prefix and rewrites the child scope's path/root_path
required_criteria_expected: a full match stops the scan and dispatches immediately
only the first partial match is retained
the partial fallback is what yields 405 rather than 404
must_not: must not describe a global argmax over numeric Match values

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A change-impact / transfer question, e.g. 'if Router.app were changed to keep scanning after a FULL match and collect all full matches, what breaks?'
reference_answer_key_points: today first FULL match short-circuits; order-dependent by design
collecting all would need a tie-break rule Starlette does not define
overlapping paths currently resolved purely by registration order
Mount/Host sub-routers would be affected because they re-enter matches()
required_criteria_expected: current behaviour is first-full-match-wins, decided by registration order
the change introduces ambiguity when two routes both return FULL
must_not: must not claim route matching is already specificity-ranked so the change is a no-op

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on when a response's background task runs and the order of multiple tasks.
reference_answer_key_points: Response.__call__ sends start+body, THEN awaits self.background
BackgroundTasks awaits tasks sequentially in add order
sync task func runs via run_in_threadpool; async awaited directly
required_criteria_expected: the background task runs after the response body is sent
BackgroundTasks runs its tasks one at a time in order
a synchronous task function runs in a threadpool
must_not: must not claim tasks run concurrently / in parallel
must not claim the task runs before or during response send

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question contrasting Response subclasses (JSONResponse / StreamingResponse / FileResponse) in how they emit the body, or how each still runs background after.
reference_answer_key_points: plain Response renders body eagerly in __init__; StreamingResponse iterates a body iterator
all of them await self.background after the body, if set
FileResponse can use zero-copy / range handling
required_criteria_expected: every response subclass awaits the background task after the body
StreamingResponse sends the body incrementally rather than all at once
must_not: must not claim StreamingResponse skips the background task

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on the split of responsibility between ExceptionMiddleware and ServerErrorMiddleware.
reference_answer_key_points: ServerErrorMiddleware outermost: unhandled -> 500, then re-raises
ExceptionMiddleware innermost: maps HTTPException/registered handlers to responses, no re-raise
ExceptionMiddleware inside user middleware -> can't catch user-middleware errors
required_criteria_expected: ServerErrorMiddleware is outermost and turns unhandled errors into 500s
ServerErrorMiddleware re-raises after responding
ExceptionMiddleware maps HTTPException to a response without re-raising
ExceptionMiddleware sits innermost, closest to the router
must_not: must not put ExceptionMiddleware outermost
must not claim ServerErrorMiddleware swallows the exception

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A change-impact question on _lookup_exception_handler's MRO walk, e.g. 'if it stopped walking __mro__ and only matched the exact class, what changes?'
reference_answer_key_points: today a handler registered for a base class catches subclasses via __mro__ walk
exact-match-only would break base-class handlers (e.g. a handler for Exception)
status-code lookup for HTTPException is unaffected (separate dict, checked first)
required_criteria_expected: the lookup currently walks the exception type's MRO so base-class handlers match
restricting to exact class would stop base-class handlers from firing
must_not: must not claim status-code handlers would also break (they're checked separately, first)

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on what the ASGI three-callable contract (scope, receive, send) is, or what starlette.types defines.
reference_answer_key_points: an ASGI app is a callable (scope, receive, send) -> awaitable
scope is a dict describing the connection; receive/send are async channels
Starlette's types module names ASGIApp/Scope/Receive/Send/Message
required_criteria_expected: an ASGI application is called with scope, receive, and send
receive and send are async callables for the message stream
must_not: must not describe a WSGI-style (environ, start_response) signature

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on what build_middleware_stack assembles and when.
reference_answer_key_points: Starlette.__call__ lazily builds the stack on first call (cached)
order: ServerErrorMiddleware -> [RequestBodyLimit] -> user middleware -> ExceptionMiddleware -> Router
built by wrapping the list in reverse
required_criteria_expected: the middleware stack is built lazily on the first request and cached
ServerErrorMiddleware ends up outermost and ExceptionMiddleware innermost
must_not: must not claim the stack is rebuilt on every request

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on why ServerErrorMiddleware is forced outermost and ExceptionMiddleware innermost rather than being ordinary user middleware.
reference_answer_key_points: ServerErrorMiddleware must see every error including from user middleware -> outermost
ExceptionMiddleware maps expected exceptions closest to the app -> innermost
user middleware sits between the two
required_criteria_expected: ServerErrorMiddleware is placed outside user middleware so it catches their errors too
ExceptionMiddleware is placed inside user middleware, next to the router
must_not: must not claim the two are interchangeable with user middleware ordering

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on the case-insensitive / immutable header and multi-dict types.
reference_answer_key_points: Headers is case-insensitive and immutable; MutableHeaders allows writes
QueryParams / FormData are immutable multi-dicts (repeated keys)
these wrap the raw ASGI byte lists
required_criteria_expected: Headers lookups are case-insensitive
QueryParams and FormData allow repeated keys (multi-dict)
must_not: must not claim Headers is a plain mutable dict

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A recall question on how TestClient runs the app without a network server.
reference_answer_key_points: httpx requests routed through an in-memory _TestClientTransport
an AnyIO portal bridges sync test code to the async app
no real socket / server process
required_criteria_expected: TestClient calls the ASGI app in-process rather than over a real socket
it uses an AnyIO portal to drive the async app from sync test code
must_not: must not claim it starts a real HTTP server on a port

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question contrasting HTTPConnection (shared base) with Request / WebSocket, or how Request.stream()/body() consume the receive channel once.
reference_answer_key_points: HTTPConnection is the read-only base (url, headers, cookies, state)
Request adds body/stream/json/form over the receive channel
stream() consumes the channel once; body() caches _body for re-reads
required_criteria_expected: HTTPConnection is the common base for Request and WebSocket
Request.stream() consumes the receive channel and can only be iterated once
must_not: must not claim body() returns an empty string on the second call (it returns the cached body)

entries.concept_label: Match enum ordering (FULL > PARTIAL > NONE) drives routing priority
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on how Router.app actually uses PARTIAL vs FULL (not on the integer values themselves).
reference_answer_key_points: FULL short-circuits the loop and dispatches
PARTIAL is only recorded (first one) and used as a fallback
that fallback is the 405 mechanism
required_criteria_expected: a FULL match immediately dispatches and ends the scan
a PARTIAL match is only a fallback used when no FULL match is found
only the first PARTIAL encountered is kept
must_not: must not present the enum integers as a global priority the router sorts on
NOTE: the concept statement's phrasing invites the argmax misconception -- a good question steers away from it

entries.concept_label: Match enum ordering (FULL > PARTIAL > NONE) drives routing priority
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A transfer question, e.g. 'two routes both return PARTIAL -- which handles the request, and how would you make a more specific route win?'
reference_answer_key_points: first PARTIAL recorded wins -> registration order again
no specificity logic exists; you would reorder routes
a FULL match anywhere later still beats any PARTIAL
required_criteria_expected: when multiple routes return PARTIAL, the first one registered is used
there is no specificity ranking; ordering is the only lever
must_not: must not invent a 'PARTIAL score' comparison

entries.concept_label: RedirectResponse uses a 302 status code by default
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A question about RedirectResponse's default status code and when to override it.
reference_answer_key_points: FOR THIS COMMIT the default is 307 (Temporary Redirect), not 302 -- see responses.py::RedirectResponse.__init__ (status_code: int = 307)
307 preserves the request method; 302 historically allowed method change to GET
callers pass status_code=301/308 for permanent redirects
required_criteria_expected: the default status code is 307
the caller can override status_code for a permanent (301/308) redirect
must_not: FACTUAL-CORRECTNESS TEST: the source concept statement says 302; a generated reference answer that repeats '302 by default' is FACTUALLY WRONG and must be scored as such. The correct default in responses.py at 4f250d6b is 307.

entries.concept_label: Request.body() reads the body once; later calls return empty
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A question on what happens when Request.body() (or .stream()) is called more than once.
reference_answer_key_points: body() caches self._body on first read and returns the SAME bytes on later calls
stream() yields the cached _body again if body() already ran
stream() raises RuntimeError('Stream consumed') only if the channel was drained WITHOUT _body being cached
required_criteria_expected: Request.body() caches the body and returns it again on subsequent calls
calling stream() after the channel is consumed (with no cached body) raises RuntimeError
must_not: FACTUAL-CORRECTNESS TEST: the source concept statement ('subsequent calls return an empty string') is wrong -- body() returns the cached bytes, not '' -- a reference answer repeating it must be scored as factually wrong.

entries.concept_label: Moving ExceptionMiddleware outside user middleware -- impact
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A change-impact question exactly on the concept: what changes for an app author if ExceptionMiddleware were placed outside user middleware.
reference_answer_key_points: today ExceptionMiddleware is innermost -> only sees router/endpoint errors
moved outside user middleware -> also catches user-middleware exceptions
an HTTPException from user middleware would then render as its 4xx not a 500
ServerErrorMiddleware stays outermost and still re-raises
registered class/status handlers unchanged
required_criteria_expected: today ExceptionMiddleware does not catch exceptions raised in user middleware
after the move it would, so a user-middleware HTTPException renders as its mapped response
ServerErrorMiddleware stays the outermost layer
must_not: must not claim it would let ExceptionMiddleware catch ServerErrorMiddleware's errors
must not claim routing/endpoint dispatch changes

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on how an endpoint's HTTPException becomes a response given the endpoint is called from Route.handle.
reference_answer_key_points: request_response wraps the endpoint call in wrap_app_handling_exceptions
Route.handle just calls self.app -- no try/except of its own
wrapper: status-code handler first, then MRO class-handler lookup, else re-raise
required_criteria_expected: the endpoint call is wrapped by wrap_app_handling_exceptions (set up in request_response)
for an HTTPException a status-code handler is checked before a class handler
if no handler matches, the wrapper re-raises
must_not: must not claim Route.handle contains the try/except
must not claim ServerErrorMiddleware renders the HTTPException

entries.concept_label: Routing & Endpoint Dispatch -> Responses & Background Tasks
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on how request_response turns a function's return value into an ASGI send, and how a returned Response's background task fits in.
reference_answer_key_points: request_response calls f(request) -> Response, then awaits response(scope, receive, send)
a sync endpoint is run via run_in_threadpool
the returned Response then emits start+body and finally awaits its background task
required_criteria_expected: request_response awaits the returned Response as an ASGI app
a synchronous endpoint function is run in a threadpool
must_not: must not claim the router serializes the response itself

entries.concept_label: Responses & Background Tasks -> Request & WebSocket Connections
entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on why a Response takes (scope, receive, send) at all, and what it uses receive for (client-disconnect detection during streaming).
reference_answer_key_points: a Response IS an ASGI app: __call__(scope, receive, send)
StreamingResponse listens on receive for http.disconnect to stop early
plain Response ignores receive
required_criteria_expected: a Response is itself an ASGI application called with scope, receive, send
StreamingResponse watches the receive channel for client disconnect
must_not: must not claim plain Response reads the request body via receive

entries.acceptable_question_shape: A comprehension question on what kind of Response ExceptionMiddleware.http_exception produces for an HTTPException.
reference_answer_key_points: http_exception returns PlainTextResponse(exc.detail, status_code=exc.status_code, headers=exc.headers)
204/304 -> a bodyless Response instead
that Response is then sent through the same send channel
required_criteria_expected: ExceptionMiddleware's default HTTPException handler returns a PlainTextResponse
the response carries the exception's status code and detail
must_not: must not claim it returns an HTML error page by default
